rule: Until Harbor renews on Oct 30, put work that helps the Harbor renewal ahead of Smart Slots and Expo work, because Harbor is 38% of revenue and is looking at a competitor before signing.

Until Harbor renews, put fixes for Harbor's two complaints, the Sep 28 sync outage and the CSV export cutoff, ahead of other Harbor work. The written outage postmortem goes first, because Dana wants it in writing.

When a deliverable is due tomorrow, put it first, even ahead of Harbor renewal work, because the deadline is immediate. For Jordan this includes the Harbor QBR deck due the day before the QBR. Harbor work follows, ahead of other Smart Slots and Expo work.

When a teammate is blocked waiting on your review or input, do that first, even ahead of Harbor renewal work, because on this team unblocking a teammate always comes first. Arjun reviews all backend PRs, so blocked PRs are his top item.

Until Harbor renews, sync-outage follow-ups (retry queue, sync error alert) count as Harbor renewal work, ahead of Smart Slots and other customers' bugs like Ridgeline duplicates, especially when Harbor will ask at the QBR. A bug in Harbor's own data still goes first.

When a customer escalates, the CEO makes the customer call herself, so it is Maya's first item. The account manager (Jordan) drops that call and stays on his own plan, even if the call ticket is assigned to him.

When a customer escalation needs an engineering fix, the on-call engineer (Nina this week) takes the escalation ticket first, then its root-cause bug. Other engineers, including Arjun, stay on their own plans even if the ticket is assigned to them, because escalations go to whoever is on call.

For Maya, until Harbor renews, Harbor renewal work comes first, then any deliverable due tomorrow (e.g. the investor update), then Smart Slots work like signing design partners, because the renewal outranks Smart Slots and the deadline is immediate.
